steps.title: Log into Snowflake UI
steps.detail: Open the Snowflake web console and sign in with your account credentials. This is the starting point for OAuth app registration (inferred).

steps.title: Navigate to OAuth Application Settings
steps.detail: In the console, go to the Settings or Account menu, select "Security" then "OAuth" and click "Create New Application" to begin registering your OAuth client (inferred).

steps.title: Enter application details and save
steps.detail: Provide a name, description, and redirect URI for your app, then save. Snowflake will generate a client ID and client secret that you can copy for use (inferred).

openQuestions.question: Where is the Snowflake developer console or portal for creating OAuth applications?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Without a known location, developers cannot begin the registration workflow.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Locate the official Snowflake documentation or support page that lists the developer console URL.

openQuestions.question: What are the step‑by‑step instructions for registering an OAuth app in Snowflake?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: The process determines the amount of manual effort and any required human interaction.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Find a guide or tutorial that outlines the registration form fields, required redirects, and any verification steps.

openQuestions.question: Does Snowflake require a review of OAuth apps before they become usable, and if so, how long does the review take?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Review time impacts the overall onboarding timeline for end‑users.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Identify any statements about app review policies, SLA, or support tickets that mention review durations.

openQuestions.question: Are there any costs (one‑time, monthly, or annual) associated with creating or maintaining an OAuth app on Snowflake?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Cost influences the feasibility for developers and their users.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Search Snowflake pricing pages or developer agreements for fees tied to API access or app registration.

openQuestions.question: What prerequisite artifacts (e.g., privacy policy URL, terms of service, verified domain) does Snowflake require for an OAuth app?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Missing required artifacts can block registration or cause later compliance issues.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Locate any developer policy documents that list required legal or technical artifacts.

openQuestions.question: Are there any human‑only blockers such as identity verification, legal signatures, or captcha that cannot be automated?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Human‑only steps increase integration complexity for AI agents.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Review the registration flow for steps that demand manual interaction beyond form filling.
